entry.title: Growing Together: Yale’s Urban Resources Initiative

media:group.media:title: Growing Together: Yale’s Urban Resources Initiative
media:group.media:description:
Every week, volunteer community groups like Friends of Edgewood Park work to protect and preserve New Haven’s parks, in partnership with the Urban Resources Initiative (URI), a nonprofit based at the Yale School of the Environment. Its work both fosters community participation in urban ecosystem management and offers Yale students opportunities to learn in the field.
Among other initiatives, for the past six years URI has supported volunteer groups in undertaking de-vining work across 17 New Haven parks, including Edgewood. With shears in hand, community members remove non-native vines and aggressive weeds from wooded areas, giving native trees an opportunity to thrive.

entry.title: What Now? Finding an American Future

media:group.media:title: What Now? Finding an American Future
media:group.media:description: This event is part Yale University’s Presidential Lecture Series. Each semester, a leading expert will visit Yale to share ideas and inspire critical thought on today's most complex topics. Marilynne Robinson is a Pulitzer Prize-winning novelist and essayist. Her novels include Housekeeping (1980), Gilead (2004), Home (2008), Lila (2014), and Jack (2020). She is also the author of many non-fiction works, articles, essays and reviews. Her most recent book, Reading Genesis, is a collection of essays that explore the literary and theological interpretations of the first book of the Bible.

entry.title: A Drizzle of Knowledge: Olive Oil Exploration

media:group.media:title: A Drizzle of Knowledge: Olive Oil Exploration
media:group.media:description:
Alongside his research in biostatistics and infectious disease epidemiology, Yale School of Public Health faculty member Tassos Kyriakides is also a certified Olive Oil Sommelier. He shares his expertise on olive oil, including its many potential health benefits, with the Yale and New Haven community multiple times a year through olive oil tastings known as “Oleotecas,” presented by the Yale Schwarzman Center.
In this video, Tassos offers a brief introduction to evaluating olive oils and selecting varieties that suit your flavor preferences. He also highlights just a few of the many ways olive oil consumption benefits human health.

media:group.media:title: Cannabis and the developing brain
media:group.media:description: As legal cannabis becomes more common and products grow more potent, what do we really know about the risks? Yale psychiatrist Deepak D'Souza explores emerging evidence on brain development, mental illness, and why some young people may be especially vulnerable. Plus, when we should think twice about the answers we get from AI chatbots (https://news.yale.edu/2026/06/12/can-we-trust-ai-models-yale-researchers-explore-roots-chatbot-errors) ; the quiet evolution of salamanders (https://news.yale.edu/2026/06/22/secret-lives-salamanders) ; and how exercise may help our bodies fight cancer (https://medicine.yale.edu/news-article/to-fight-cancer-try-adding-exercise/) .

entry.title: An astrophysicist and a musician on waves

media:group.media:title: An astrophysicist and a musician on waves
media:group.media:description:
An astrophysicist and a musician walk into a bar. One topic. Different points of view. Many unexpected connections.
Walk Into a Bar unites two experts in wildly different fields and invites them to grapple with a single theme they both care about. An unscripted conversation follows. Everyone — even the experts — learns something new.
In the first episode, Chiara Mingarelli, an astrophysicist, and Maiani da Silva, a musician, explore gravitational waves and sound waves. Watch as they find a meeting point in Pythagoras; discuss the overlap between the arts and the sciences; and broach what it really means to pass the test of time.
Walk Into a Bar is produced by Yale’s Office of Public Affairs and Communications. Episodes are recorded at a bar on the Yale University campus. Learn more at news.yale.edu.
